identity.name: Propane-1,2-diol esters of fatty acids
synonyms: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids
Propylene glycol mono- and diesters of fats and fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Mixture of propylene glycol mono- and di-esters of edible fatty acids (non-ionic emulsifier)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic ester molecules reduce oil-water interfacial tension and improve emulsion stability and texture in fat-containing foods.

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 confirmed 25 mg/kg bw/day expressed as propane-1,2-diol, corresponding to 80 mg/kg bw/day for E477 (max 31% free+bound propane-1,2-diol in specification).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported use levels; refined non-brand-loyal exposure estimates did not exceed ADI.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw, expressed as/as propylene glycol.

concerns.summary: EFSA identified data gaps: no chronic toxicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive, or developmental studies directly on E477; EFSA also recommended tighter impurity/specification limits (toxic elements, trans fatty acids, glycidyl/3-MCPD esters, erucic acid).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no genotoxicity concern for E477 based on available in vitro data and related propane-1,2-diol evidence.
Short-term animal studies reported by EFSA showed no adverse effects at highest tested doses.
EFSA refined non-brand-loyal exposure estimates were below the E477 ADI across population groups.

populations: children (highest modeled intake, still below ADI)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported high (P95) refined exposure up to 16.7 mg/kg bw/day in children, below the 80 mg/kg bw/day ADI for E477; EFSA flagged future need to consider combined propane-1,2-diol exposure from E477, E1520, and E405.

risk_assessment.rationale: E477 is approved by EFSA/FDA/JECFA with ADI-based control and no current-use safety concern in EFSA refined exposure estimates, but direct long-term endpoint data are limited and specification-related uncertainties remain.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation confirmed ADI and concluded no safety concern at reported use levels.
FDA permits use under 21 CFR 172.856 with GMP-like quantitative condition (reasonably required amount).
JECFA ADI (0-25 mg/kg bw as propylene glycol) supports long-standing risk-management basis.
No IARC listing for this additive found in the current classifications dataset.
Important data gaps exist for chronic/carcinogenicity/reproductive/developmental endpoints directly on E477.
